remediation.strategy: Tie GUI burst state to the container lifecycle. In end_desktop, and in the pause, resume and restore paths (API and web), close the burst and then clear _gui_input_at and _gui_snap_at, so the next GUI input always snapshots and opens a burst on the current container. Record the container_id in the burst and close a burst whose container_id no longer matches without killing anything. Skip paused sandboxes in close_idle_gui_bursts, or close the burst before pausing. In _close_gui_burst, remove the burst only after stray stop and the manifest diff succeed, and log a gui_burst_close_failed event otherwise. Add regression tests: GUI input soon after restore opens a new burst, a burst idling out while paused is kept or closed before pausing, and a burst opened before a container swap does not kill the new desktop.

likelihood.reason: Pausing or restoring a sandbox while the agent is active on the GUI is the natural human reaction to suspicious activity. The pause variant only needs the pause to outlast gui_snapshot_idle (60 s) while the sandbox page is open, or while any other caller runs close_idle_gui_bursts. For the restore variant, the agent keeps the timers recent just by issuing frequent inputs. It needs no active human lease at restore.

impact.reason: It defeats the only compensating controls on the GUI approval bypass (N-1). An agent-started uid-1001 background process survives indefinitely, and its /workspace changes are missing from gui_changes, so the audit trail the human relies on after a restore or pause is incomplete. The restore variant also skips the post-restore GUI restore point. No privilege beyond the sandbox and no network (network_mode none). A same-root-cause stale baseline can also kill the new desktop session, but only through a race and pid divergence, and it was shown only in the harness.

confidence.reason: The restore variant is pure control-plane state logic in service.py and was reproduced with the real AgentBox, AuditLog, Policy, DesktopControl and gui_strays. Clearing the timers (the proposed fix) restores the kill and the logging. The pause variant's decisive step is the source-visible _require_running status check. The harness fakes SandboxManager and does not exercise live Docker pids, the real xfce process tree, or the stale-baseline race timing. Those affect only the related desktop-kill consequence, not the confirmed stray-survival and missing-log result.

title: Web exec approval card renders the agent's command with raw Unicode bidi controls, letting a prompt-injected agent spoof the human approver's view of what will run
description:
The web approval card shows the agent-submitted exec command in 
{{ a.args.command }}
under Jinja HTML autoescape only (markupsafe.escape only touches & < > ' "). Unicode bidirectional controls (U+202A-E, U+2066-9) survive escaping and are rendered live by the browser, which reorders the displayed text. The terminal approver (cli.py _show_approval) prints the same command through cli._safe, which turns those code points into visible \uXXXX escapes, so only the web approval path is affected. For non-allowlisted programs (sh/python3) the policy requires approval and the system preview computes no affected paths (sandbox.preview only handles rm/curl segments), adding a note that directs the approver to read the command text itself. A prompt-injected agent (lowest-trust agent token, assumed in the threat model) can therefore submit a Trojan-Source-laid-out command whose rendered form on the web card reads as a single benign echo while a separate approval-gated program actually executes, defeating the human's exec-approval review.
root_cause: _approvals.html:8 relies on HTML autoescape, which neutralises markup but not Unicode bidi/control characters; the web UI has no equivalent of cli._safe (cli.py:34-39) for approval args, and base.html:23's pre style applies no unicode-bidi isolation. The terminal path escapes these characters (cli.py:196-199) but the web path does not, so the two human-facing surfaces disagree about the same command.
intended_behavior: Both human approval surfaces should show the agent-chosen command with display-reordering and control characters neutralised, so the approver's decision is bound to the exact command that will execute. The code already does this for the terminal approver via cli._safe; the web card should apply the same neutralisation.

conditions.description: Attacker is a prompt-injected per-sandbox agent token (agt_), the lowest-trust network principal, acting on its own sandbox.

A human reviews and approves the exec via the web UI approval card; the terminal approver (cli.py) escapes the bidi controls and is not affected, and the approver must not notice the reordered rendering.

Add a Jinja filter that maps C0/C1/DEL and bidi controls (the cli._UNSAFE set) to visible escapes, and apply it to the exec command, preview effect/path cells, and describe() output on the approval and audit templates; optionally also wrap the <pre> in CSS unicode-bidi: isolate/plaintext as defence in depth. likelihood.reason: The threat model assumes a prompt-injected agent, and embedding bidi isolates in an exec command is trivial. It requires the human to approve via the web UI (the terminal path escapes the controls) and to not notice the reordered rendering, which bounds likelihood below high.

impact.reason: Defeats the human exec-approval boundary (the primary control between a prompt-injected agent and arbitrary non-allowlisted exec) via display spoofing, yielding agent-chosen arbitrary in-sandbox code execution (python3/sh) under the human's misdirected approval. Contained by the sandbox isolation (network=none, dropped caps, no-new-privileges, runc); it is not by itself a host, cross-sandbox, or human-token compromise.

confidence.reason: Source establishes the asymmetry end to end: cli._safe escapes the bidi set (cli.py:34, 196-199) while _approvals.html:8 autoescapes only (base.html:23 adds no isolation), and sandbox.preview lists nothing for python3/sh so the command text is the sole basis. The parent's real Chromium reproduction (l5_card.png / l5.out) demonstrates the concrete visual spoof, and my own sbx check confirms escaping preserves the controls. Both candidate blockers are resolved; the only part I could not run myself is the browser render, which the parent supplied.

title: Cookie-authenticated web UI and desktop page set no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, so a same-site origin can frame /ui/sandboxes/{sid} (or the desktop page) and a single disguised click approves a pending agent action or takes over the desktop
description: No agentbox HTML response sets CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, api.build installs no middleware, and Caddy is a bare reverse_proxy, so every cookie-authenticated page is frameable. The session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only and Path=/ (not port-scoped). A pure cross-site framer is blocked by SameSite=Strict (confirmed: the parent-live control framed from http://localhost:9999 and the frame fell back to /login). But a same-site origin -- another port on the same loopback host in local mode, or a sibling subdomain under the same registrable domain in proxy mode -- is same-site, so the browser sends the full-scope session cookie into a transparent iframe of /ui/sandboxes/{sid}#approvals. The approve/deny/snapshot buttons and the desktop takeover button are single-click (no hx-confirm; only restore/delete use hx-confirm). Because the click originates inside the framed agentbox document, the htmx/fetch POST carries Origin == Host, so same_origin() passes (it also allows a missing Origin), and box.decide(...actor='human') runs the agent's originally-gated args as a human-approved action. A prompt-injected agent controls its pending card text and can learn its sandbox id, aiding a same-site decoy in positioning the button. Parent-live Chromium confirmed the mechanics end-to-end; what remains unverified is whether a real deployment exposes a same-site origin an attacker can influence.
claimed_root_cause: Cookie-authenticated HTML (render() in web.py sets only Cache-Control/X-AB-Version; desktop_page sets only Cache-Control; Caddyfile adds no headers; no middleware in api.build) carries no framing policy, and the state-changing UI actions rely only on SameSite=Strict plus same_origin() -- neither of which stops a same-site framer or a click induced inside the framed agentbox document. SameSite=Strict blocks only genuinely cross-site framers; it does not scope by port or subdomain, so a same-site origin defeats it.

trace.description: Full authenticated UI page served (render()) with only Cache-Control/X-AB-Version; no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, so it can be embedded in a cross-origin iframe.
Session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, host-only, default Path=/, not port-scoped; sent on same-site cross-port / sibling-subdomain iframe loads (SameSite blocks only cross-site).
Approvals fragment auto-loaded into the framed page (hx-get every 2s), rendering the pending approval card with its action buttons.
Single-click hx-post /ui/approvals/{aid}/approve with hx-disabled-elt but no hx-confirm; one framed click suffices.
An in-frame POST from the framed agentbox document has Origin == Host (and a missing Origin is also allowed), so same_origin() returns True.
Browser-session route (browser_human) calls box.decide(aid, approve=True, actor='human', session=p.session).
_run_tool(sid, tool, args) runs the agent's originally gated args as a human-approved action.

evidence.description: render() TemplateResponse sets only Cache-Control: no-store (plus X-AB-Version at line 92); no framing header. Grep over agentbox/ and deploy/ finds no X-Frame-Options/CSP/frame-ancestors and no add_middleware.
desktop_page returns HTMLResponse(D.page(...)) with only Cache-Control: no-store; the takeover/handback controls live in this frameable page.
Proxy mode is a bare reverse_proxy agentbox:8765 adding no response headers, so proxy deployments also lack framing headers.
agentbox frames its own desktop page (iframe src=/sandboxes/{sid}/desktop), so a correct fix must be frame-ancestors 'self' / X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, not DENY.
Deny is also single-click; only restore/delete carry hx-confirm (sandbox.html:5, _snapshots.html), so approve/deny/snapshot/takeover are inducible with one blind click.
Desktop takeover button posts /takeover with no confirmation; combined with the frameable desktop page this clickjacks screen control.

screen_principal enforces only same_origin after the cookie lookup; a framed agentbox document satisfies it, so same_origin + SameSite=Strict are the only barriers and neither stops a same-site framer.

blockers: Decisive deployment fact, outside source/local observation: whether a given deployment exposes an attacker-influenceable same-site origin -- another port on the same loopback host in local mode, or a sibling subdomain under the same registrable domain in proxy mode. SameSite=Strict blocks every pure cross-site framer (parent-live control: framing from http://localhost:9999 produced a frame that fell back to /login), and the assumed local attacker (a prompt-injected agent in a network_mode=none container) cannot itself bind a host port to create such an origin, so exploitation depends on an independent same-site foothold that source cannot establish.

Cross-engine browser-policy behavior: the parent's real Chromium (agents/parent-live/artifacts/l3) is the decisive reproduction, not mine (jinja2/no browser in my sbx) -- it observed Chromium sending the SameSite=Strict host-only cookie into a same-site cross-port iframe and the in-frame htmx POST completing (apr_0fb8e904e830 -> executed, decided_by human). Firefox/WebKit same-site-cross-port iframe cookie behavior remains unobserved.

validation_plan.local: Already executed by the parent on loopback and reproducible: start the app with the fake-Docker shim via uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8765 with a dummy human token; in Playwright Chromium (and additionally Firefox/WebKit) log in, create a pending exec approval for a dummy sandbox; serve evil.html from http://127.0.0.1:9999 with a decoy over an opacity-reduced iframe of /ui/sandboxes/{sid}#approvals; assert the frame URL stays on /ui/sandboxes/{sid} (not /login) and that clicking the decoy over the approve button yields approval status=executed, decided_by=human (parent-live l3.out shows exactly this for Chromium). Repeat for the desktop page takeover button. Control (must fail): serve from http://localhost:9999 (cross-site) -> frame redirects to /login (parent-live confirmed). Regression: add middleware setting X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN + CSP frame-ancestors 'self' and confirm the external frame is blocked while the in-app /sandboxes/{sid}/desktop iframe still loads.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner runs curl -sI against deployed /ui, /login, /ui/sandboxes/{sid} and /sandboxes/{sid}/desktop to confirm no X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors are present (local, direct-TLS, and Caddy proxy modes), and enumerates same-host loopback ports and sibling subdomains under the same registrable domain that serve attacker-influenceable or XSS-prone content; the finding is exploitable only if at least one such same-site origin exists.
